subject: monsterTruck
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: monster truck with huge tyres.
Style: pixel art.
reasoning:
I'm planning a single TypeScript module for a pixel-art vehicle prop, using joints for the chassis and wheels so parts can be rigged and rotate, keeping the rest of the structure simple.

Working out realistic monster truck proportions—large tires with tread lugs, chrome hubs, chassis rails, leaf springs and shocks, and a raised body with cab, hood, bed, bumpers, headlights, exhaust stacks, roll-bar, and flame decals—all placed and scaled with pixel-texture detailing in mind.

I'm sketching the overall skeleton: a root chassis joint at mid-height with wheel joints positioned at each axle, oriented along the axle axis, so each wheel part can be parented and animated independently.

For textures I'm planning a tire tread pattern — a dark rubber cylinder with small lug blocks ringed around the outside, facing outward to simulate tread detail without being too complex to generate.

I need to figure out the ring placement along the axle using the wheel joint's position and axis, since the joint likely has no child bone to derive length from. I'll construct the line endpoints manually from the wheel center offset along the axle direction, and explicitly pass the wheel bone reference rather than relying on automatic nearest-bone detection.

For the sidewall decal, I'm designing a pixel texture for the tire using concentric rings by radial distance—gold hub center, silver rim, bolt lugs, rubber sidewall, and a dark tread ring—placed as a circle facing outward on each wheel side.

Now I'm setting wheel dimensions: radius 0.85, tire width 0.9, with inner and outer face offsets giving a total width around 3.8, close enough to a real monster truck's ~3.6. I'm placing front and rear axles at z=±1.5 for a 3m wheelbase, and sizing the body length to roughly span -2.3 to 2.3 along z to resemble an overhanging pickup-style monster truck body.

I'm setting up the chassis root joint at [0,1.2,0], then laying out wheel joints as children without specific role names, and defining the chassis rails as two dark iron-colored boxes offset at x=±0.55, spanning the full body length, using pixel-style cell paint rather than the clockwork kit's metal paints to keep the look consistent.

Now I'm adding the suspension system: front/rear axle boxes positioned at wheel height, a differential pumpkin at center, four angled coilover shocks running from axle to chassis using yellow rods with chrome inner rods, four-link suspension bars, and driveshaft rods — then moving on to the body color scheme of bright red with yellow flames and blue accents.

I'm settling on a red (#d8281e) body with orange/yellow flame decals and black trim, using pixel-style cell shading with three-tone shading based on surface normals. For the body geometry, I'm building a lower body slab box on the chassis for the doors and sides, then adding flame texture planes on the side panels to create rising flame decals along the front lower section.

Now I'm working out flame texture orientation on each side — using a transparent-background pixel texture so the body color shows through, then calculating the correct direction vectors so flames on the left panel point toward the rear and flames on the right panel orient correctly based on each plane's facing direction.

For the right side I'm planning to either flip the geometry with a negative scale or build a mirrored draw function that reflects the x-coordinate across the texture width. Then I'm roughing out the hood geometry with box dimensions and positions for the lower body slab, hood top, and front grille.

Adding grille texture, headlights, and bumper...

Defining the bed section now, placing sidewalls and tailgate above a solid floor slab, then considering a roll bar over the bed and wheel arch cutouts where tires poke through the body.

Adding fender flares positioned above the tires, connected to the body edges to avoid collision with the wheels, finishing with red paneling and black rim trim before moving on to roof lights.

Now I'm adding a light bar with six glowing yellow boxes on the cab roof, chrome exhaust stacks mounted behind the cab, a thin antenna with a small flag, glowing red tail lights, side mirrors, and a pixel-art license plate reading "MUD 4 U."

Skipping text decals since drawing letters is too heavy for the pixel kit, I decide to add a simple pixel-art skull emblem on the cab door instead. I'm listing out the textures I'll need: tire sidewall, flame decals for both sides, grille, headlight, windshield, side window, skull emblem, and light bar, plus paint colors for rubber, body, chrome, frame, and yellow trim.

Writing a helper function for creating boxes...

Still writing tire texture logic...

For the body geometry, I'm sizing the tire cylinder and lugs so they protrude slightly beyond the ring radius, then nudging the wheel's vertical center to compensate for that small overhang.

For the ring of lugs, I'm working out the right fromDeg/toDeg spacing for a 16-count ring so the staggered row's offsets land evenly without duplicating endpoints, using a step of 22.5 degrees starting at 11.25.

I'm placing the two lug rows at axle offsets of about ±0.225 to fit within the cylinder's 0.9 width, matching the lug geometry dimensions. For coloring the rubber, I'm sketching a generic shading helper that paints cells based on surface normal plus some random jitter, so I can reuse it for both the rubber texture and the body paint.

For the body paint, I'm defining a dark lower trim band using a height cutoff around y<1.45, with darker colors below and red tones above, planning to apply it broadly since the bumper gets painted separately anyway. Then I'm moving into generating the flame decal texture for the sides of the body — setting up a grid, defining tongues of flame with a centerline that wavers using a sine function, and working out how to mirror the pattern for the opposite side.

Writing flame shape math...

I'm adding a dark outline on tip edges, then handling left/right side mirroring so flames point toward the rear depending on viewer position. Next I'm defining the windshield texture with sky-blue color, diagonal white glare streaks, and a dark frame border, plus similar side window textures.

Now I'm sketching out the remaining parts: a generic window texture function with an optional pillar, a grille with silver bars and a red badge, glowing headlights, a skull decal, chrome shading, a light bar with glowing yellow boxes, and a small antenna flag on a rod, importing a glow effect from the kit.

Setting up wheel joints and hub details now, naming them FL/FR etc. with positions based on chassis width, and adding a protruding gold hubcap cylinder at the wheel center.

Now working on shocks: computing lower and upper mount points for each axle/side, using rods for the shock body and small cylinder discs stacked along the shock to fake coil spring detail.

I'm checking whether shocks collide with the body geometry — shock travel runs roughly from y=0.9 up to 1.55, and since the body bottom sits around 1.35-1.4, part of the shock would be hidden inside the body, which is fine visually. I'm adjusting chassis rail height to 1.1 (top at 1.24) so the body bottom at 1.4 leaves a visible gap showing the rails, and setting the lower slab to span y 1.4-2.1 centered at 1.75 with 0.7 height. I'm skipping the skid plate and body risers for now, and starting on the 4-link suspension rods connecting from the axle at x±0.35, y 0.86.

Now I'm adding the differential housing as a small dark metal box centered on the axle, a drive shaft rod running along the centerline with a chassis crossmember, and figuring out the rod/bone syntax for attaching these parts to the chassis. I'm also planning skull decals on the cab doors, positioning them on the side planes near the cab width.

Now I'm placing flame decals on the rear quarter panels, sizing the plane to match the texture's aspect ratio and positioning it along the front body length, with a skull decal placed lower on the rear quarter at a smaller scale.

Working through cab window placement: side windows, windshield, and rear window planes sized to pixel texture dimensions, positioned flush against the cab's side walls and front/rear faces. I'm also reconciling the cab width against the body's lower slab width, adjusting the side window x-offsets accordingly, then sizing and positioning the hood to bridge the gap between the cab front and the body's forward edge.

Now I'm placing the roof box above the windshield, then adding a hood-mounted supercharger assembly made of a chrome box with a dark intake scoop on top, plus small stacks for detail. Moving on to sketch the fender slabs next.

Still placing body details...

Now adding exhaust stacks in the bed with cylindrical pipes and glowing orange flame cones at the tips, a chrome roll hoop with rods and crossbar, and mirror boxes positioned near the cab.

I'm also planning the antenna with a small flag box, deciding to trim its height to keep the total proportions more truck-realistic, and skipping underbody skirts for simplicity. Setting a texel size for the paint cells before moving into writing the actual code.
